why: The pre-registered WBC arm ran a fixed 1750-update horizon. Its dev diagnostics are monotone in the horizon and reverse sign: Pearson +0.419 / sign 0.645 / nMSE 0.920 at 250 updates, decaying through +0.250, +0.074, -0.028, -0.143, -0.144 to -0.152 at 1750, while the mean per-response log-ratio to the reference falls from -0.75 to -6.68. The finite-pool target is therefore neurally realizable on unseen prompts early in training, and the weighted-behaviour-cloning objective then keeps sharpening past it. A shorter horizon is a different experiment, not a re-read of this one.
selection_rule: The horizon is chosen on the dev split of the same pool construction, from the already-recorded eval trajectory of wbc_primary_v1. No test prompt, no downstream benchmark and no generation output participates in this choice. This arm is reported as dev-selected and never as the pre-registered primary.

changed.lr_schedule: cosine over the declared horizon, so the shorter arm anneals over its own 250 updates rather than truncating the long arm's schedule; this is a real difference between the arms and is reported as such

reporting_contract: The 1750-update arms remain the matched primary comparison and are reported in full whatever they show.
This arm is an additional row, labelled dev-selected horizon.
Its downstream evaluation uses the same frozen generation and scoring protocol as the primary arms.
If it fails, the failure is reported; the horizon is not searched further tonight.
